# University of the Andes (Colombia) — Concise Summary
The University of the Andes (Universidad de los Andes, Uniandes) was founded in 1948 in Bogotá as Colombia’s first nonsectarian and non-politically affiliated university, inspired by American models and intellectual movements advocating modernization and technical education. It began with 80 students and a few faculties, quickly growing in size and reputation, providing both technical and liberal education. The institution is governed by a Board of Trustees and Board of Directors, with a structure defined in its statutes and a mission focused on autonomy, academic excellence, pluralism, and fostering critical, ethical educational development.
Uniandes offers interdisciplinary studies across 10 faculties and several academic units, with flexible curricula allowing students to design their own academic paths. Known for its highly qualified faculty—most with PhDs from top international universities—the university has a prominent student body, with 95% of undergraduates from the top 1% of Colombian high school students and 30% from outside Bogotá. The campus, located in the historical center of Bogotá, comprises renovated buildings and modern facilities, including libraries, laboratories, sports facilities (La Caneca), and amenities supporting student life and research. Uniandes maintains political neutrality and nurtures international exchange, with partnerships linking it to over 119 universities in 34 countries. Notable alumni include Colombian national leaders, academics, artists, and scientists. The university mascot is Seneca the goat, symbolizing community tradition and spirit.
